title: Qonclave common definitions
description: Shared types referenced by every other Qonclave v1 schema. See docs/COMMUNICATION.md for the prose and dictionary.md for the enumerated values.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the Qonclave wire contract this document conforms to. A receiver MUST reject a major version it does not implement, and MUST tolerate unknown fields within a version it does.

nodeId.description: Stable identifier for a node, assigned at commissioning. Unique within a tenant.

tenantId.description: Isolation boundary. Nodes of different tenants MUST NOT exchange events, and a capability grant is denied across tenants unless explicitly scoped.

nodeType.description: Role a node currently fills. A node may change role at runtime (hub election), so this is state, not identity.

profile.description: Conformance profile the node implements. See spec/v1/profiles/.

timestamp.description: Absolute time, RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 with an explicit offset.

relativeTime.description: Time as reported by a device with no trustworthy clock. A duty-cycled device that deep-sleeps for a day cannot produce a reliable absolute timestamp, so it reports its own wake counter instead and the receiving hub stamps authoritative time. Devices on the `minimal` profile MAY use this in place of `timestamp`.

wake_counter.description: Monotonic count of wake cycles since commissioning. Never resets except on re-commissioning.

ms_since_wake.description: Milliseconds elapsed within the current wake window.

uncertainty_s.description: Device's own estimate of clock drift, if it has one. Omit if unknown.

mediaPayload.description: An attached sensor sample. OPTIONAL on every message: a temperature sensor has a reading, not a frame. On the `minimal` profile this is normally absent, since a LoRa frame cannot carry base64 media.

media_type.description: IANA media type of the decoded payload.

data_encoding.description: How `data` is encoded. `base64` in JSON; `raw` when the container is CBOR and the value is a byte string.

power.description: Measured power state, used by placement to decide whether this node should run inference locally. Reported by any node that can measure it; a mains-powered hub reports on_mains=true and omits battery_pct.

thermal_headroom_c.description: Degrees C below the throttling threshold. Zero or negative means the node is throttling and should not be given heavy work.

duty_cycle_s.description: For duty-cycled devices: nominal seconds between wakes. 86400 for a daily sensor. Absent for always-on nodes.

load.description: Current utilization, broadcast in the discovery manifest so a hub can route work to the least busy compute node.

capabilities.description: What this node can actually do. Placement filters candidate tiers against this before asking the developer's policy to choose.

complexity.description: Ordered class of model a task needs. Ordering is significant: a node advertising max_complexity=detect cannot serve a vlm_reason task.

privacy.description: Egress constraint the framework enforces regardless of what a placement policy returns. `no_egress` forbids a shared multi-tenant compute node; `local_only` forbids leaving the originating device at all.

taskDescriptor.description: What the application declares about an inference task, as opposed to what the framework measures about nodes. Travels with an escalated event so the receiving tier can re-plan against the same intent.

use_case.description: Free-form application tag. The framework never interprets this; a placement policy may.

deadline_ms.description: Total budget for the task, set once by the originating node.

remaining_ms.description: Budget left at the moment of sending. MUST be decremented by each tier before escalating. Without this every tier re-plans against the original deadline and the ladder silently blows its own SLA.

hops.description: Tiers already visited, in order. Used to detect loops and to attribute latency.

signature.description: Detached signature over the canonical encoding of the enclosing document, excluding this field. Algorithm is determined by the issuer's key type, established at commissioning.
